title: Stability channel policy and support matrix for runtime, API, SDK, console
creator: Maya Patel
description: Define a pragmatic Stability Channel (long-term-stability) policy and an operational support matrix covering the serving runtime, public API, official SDKs, and Console UI. This ticket formalizes versioning rules, upgrade paths, rollout gates, and the automation needed to safely support customers on long-lived channels while allowing rapid innovation on the Current channel.
rationale: Engineering and GTM teams need a single, actionable source of truth for what guarantees we make for long-running customer deployments (Dedicated/Private) versus the hosted API. Current ad-hoc decisions cause upgrade confusion, inconsistent SDK behavior, and reactive rollbacks. A clear matrix enables predictable SLAs, precise deprecation timelines, and automation for safer rollouts.
scope: Design the channel taxonomy; define per-surface compatibility (runtime binary/weights, REST API surface, SDK minor/major rules, Console feature flags); specify support durations, security patch policy, and rollback criteria. Produce runnable upgrade playbooks and small automation components: compatibility checker, SDK preflight CI job, release gating alerts.
out_of_scope: Full implementation of the upgrade agent for on-prem customers (separate implementation ticket), migration UI polish in Console beyond rollout indicators, contractual changes to enterprise SLAs.
compatibility_matrix_summary: Three-channel model: Experimental (fastest cadence, no stability guarantees), Current (regular cadence, backward-compatible minor versions within same major), Stability (18-month security + critical-fix support; only critical patches and security backports; explicit upgrade windows). Rules: runtime major bumps are breaking; API minor bumps must be backward compatible for Current; Stability only receives patch-level API compat and documented opt-ins for proto changes. SDKs: patch and minor maintain backward compatibility within a major for Current; Stability SDKs receive ABI-compatible patches and compatibility shims where feasible.
rollout_gates: Pre-release: automated compatibility checker must pass for runtime and SDKs
Canary: <1% traffic for 6 hours with no elevated 5xx or latency P95 regressions (>15%)
Ramp: progressive increases with automated health checks; abort if error rate delta >2% or user-facing latencies P95 increase >10%
Post-release: 72h stability window monitored by ReleaseOps with nightly regression snapshot
rollout_playbook: Stage artifacts into release channel namespace (runtime images, API schema tags, SDK packages)
Run compatibility checker across pinned customer models and stored prompt sets
Enable canary for runtime in a dedicated shard and route small percentage of traffic
Monitor tracing, cost-per-token, KV cache hit-rate, and error budgets; escalate to on-call if thresholds breached
If abort: trigger automatic fallback to previous runtime image and open rollback PRs for SDK packages
automation_requirements: compatibility-checker service (static API/schema compare + runtime smoke tests)
SDK preflight CI job that runs against the current API surface and runtime dev image
ReleaseOps alerting playbook integrated into PagerDuty + Slack channel
Console rollout widget that displays channel membership and upgrade availability
acceptance_criteria: A public-facing Support Matrix document exists describing guarantees per channel for each surface
Compatibility checker prototype that validates API schema changes and a runtime smoke test harness
A documented gating policy with objective thresholds and a tested canary-to-ramp sequence
Automation hooks created in CI to block breaking SDK releases with failing preflight checks
Security review completed and signoff recorded for Stability channel patch process
